title: What is halal?
description: What does halal mean in food? Understand ingredients, label information and the limits of BOTIA’s assessment compared with halal certification.
lead: Halal means permitted under Islamic law. In food, it refers to both ingredients and the conditions in which food is prepared and handled.
food_text: The Codex guidelines cover lawful sources, preparation, processing, transport and storage. An ingredient list can show declared ingredients, but cannot by itself establish that all these requirements are met.
criteria_text: No prohibited ingredients or doubtful origin detected on the label.
uncertainty_text: When the label does not establish the origin or process, BOTIA uses Mashbooh (doubt). Missing information is not proof that an ingredient is Halal or Haram.
limits_title: What BOTIA can and cannot conclude
can1: Read declared ingredients from the label.
can2: Detect clearly Haram ingredients based on documented criteria.
can3: Detect ingredients with ambiguous origin and make the silence visible.
cannot1: Certify Halal — it is not a guarantee or seal of approval.
cannot2: Detect undeclared processes like cross-contamination in factories.
cannot3: Replace a religious authority or certification body.
